keyboard.action: Move focus to the segment visually to the right.
Move focus to the segment visually to the left.
Increase the focused segment by one, wrapping within its range; on an empty segment start from the placeholder value.
Decrease the focused segment by one, wrapping within its range.
Increase the focused segment by a larger step.
Decrease the focused segment by a larger step.
Set the focused segment to its minimum.
Set the focused segment to its maximum.
Remove the last typed digit of the focused segment; when it becomes empty show the placeholder; on an already empty segment move to the previous segment.

A digit (in any digit set the locale accepts) is appended to the focused segment; when no further digit could be valid, focus advances to the next segment. Letters match a month name or day period by prefix.
Move to the next segment, then out of the field; each segment is a tab stop.

focus.entry: The first segment in visual start order.
focus.tabStops: One per editable segment. (MUI X offers the alternative of a single tab stop with arrow movement between sections.)

rtlDecisions.question: In a segmented date or time field in RTL, which segment does ArrowLeft move to?
rtlDecisions.apg: No segmented-field page. Each segment is a spinbutton, whose page binds only vertical arrows.

libraries.behaviour: In RTL the group finds the neighbouring segment by geometry (bounding rectangles), not DOM order, so ArrowLeft goes to the segment visually on the left.
ArrowRight moves to the section recorded as the right-hand neighbour in a visual section order computed with isRtl.
The masked input moves the cell index by -1 on ArrowLeft and +1 on ArrowRight with no direction test.

rtlDecisions.reason: Numeric date and time segments form left-to-right runs inside right-to-left text, so DOM order and visual order disagree in ways a simple swap cannot express. The key must move to the segment it points at; the engine resolves that from the rendered order.

data.notes: RTL is the hard part of this pattern. A numeric date such as 11/11/2026 is a left-to-right run even inside right-to-left text, while a date with a month name in Arabic lays its segments out right-to-left; the segment order in the DOM is the locale's logical order in both cases. So "ArrowLeft = previous" is wrong, and "ArrowLeft = next" is wrong: the key must go to the segment that is visually on that side (rtl: visual). React Aria finds the neighbour by bounding rectangle in RTL; MUI X precomputes visual neighbours. For a test, assert against rendered positions: after ArrowLeft the focused segment's left edge is smaller than before. Typing accepts Latin, Arabic-Indic and Extended Arabic-Indic digits regardless of the digits displayed. Auto-advance after a complete segment follows logical order (day, then month, then year for ar locales), not visual side.
